reasons: Only four of seven sections were available to review.
The array area appears to assume watts while the input is labelled kWdc, which needs verifying.
Some drawing hooks run after an early return; this is safe only because the parent screen checks the data first.

terms.meaning: Direct current from the panels and alternating current sent to the grid.
Balance of system, the non-panel parts of an installation.
The middle value of a cost range, used as the box's headline cost.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the diagram
sections.what: Brings in the diagram library and its style sheet, the animation library, icons, and the store.
sections.why: Likely reason: the diagram library supplies the boxes, arrows and controls that are used here.
sections.watch_out: Without the diagram library's style sheet, the boxes and arrows will not be drawn with their correct look.

sections.name: SchematicView (part 1)
sections.title: Module, inverter, and grid boxes
sections.what: Works out each box's cost and basic dimensions, then defines the modules, inverters, and electrical BOS and grid boxes, each with an icon and detail values. The module box also shows an estimated array area.
sections.why: Likely reason: each box shows the figure the user would compare with the results tab.
sections.watch_out: The array area divides by 1000, which suggests the code expects watts, yet the system size is labelled kWdc, so the area may be off by a factor of 1000.

sections.name: SchematicView (part 2)
sections.title: Storage and total cost boxes
sections.what: Adds the energy storage box when storage is on, showing hours, capacity in kWh, and efficiency. Then adds a total cost box, placed lower when storage is included.
sections.why: Storage is optional, so its box appears only when the run includes it.
sections.watch_out: The total box's detail is named msp but holds a formatted median total, so the label may mislead.

sections.name: SchematicView (part 3)
sections.title: Arrows and selection state
sections.what: Defines the arrows: modules to inverters (DC power), inverters to grid (AC power), and an extra arrow to storage when storage is on. Then sets up the box and arrow state and a click handler that records the selected box.
sections.why: Likely reason: the arrows show the direction the power flows.
sections.watch_out: The early return above these hooks is safe only because the Dashboard shows this screen only when outputs exist; changing that check could crash the page.

sections.name: SchematicView (part 4)
sections.title: Flow diagram and component details
sections.what: Draws the flow diagram of cost parts on the left and a 'Component Details' card on the right. Clicking a part fills the card with its name, icon, and cost per kWdc, except that the total part shows no per-unit cost line in the header. A zoom control panel and a small overview map sit in the diagram corner.
sections.why: Likely reason: the picture and the numbers sit side by side in one grid so both are visible on wide screens. Reason not stated in the code for the fixed 600 pixel diagram height.
sections.watch_out: The card header assumes every non-total part has a numeric cost, so a part without one would break the page.

sections.name: SchematicView (part 5)
sections.title: Listing the selected part's details
sections.what: Lists every detail of the selected part as a label and value pair. Camel-case field names are turned into spaced words, and numbers are shown with up to three decimal places. For the total, it adds a bold line with the median cost per kWdc.
sections.why: Likely reason: the rows are built from whatever fields the data contains, so new fields appear without changing this code.
sections.watch_out: The labels come straight from the data's field names, so renaming a field changes what the user reads.

sections.name: CustomNode, nodeTypes
sections.title: Box look and diagram box type
sections.what: Defines how each box in the diagram looks: a green-bordered card with an icon, name, and cost per kWdc, with a solid green fill for the total. Each box has connection points on its left and right for arrows, and it grows slightly on hover. The mapping that tells the diagram to use this look is set once at module level.
sections.why: The code comment says the mapping is defined at module level so the diagram does not redraw every box on each refresh.
sections.watch_out: Moving the mapping inside the component, or giving a non-total box no numeric cost, would slow or break the diagram.

summary: An interactive diagram of the solar system showing the modules, inverters, electrical BOS and grid, and optionally storage and a total cost box, each showing its cost.
purpose: Shows how the parts connect and what each one costs, so the user can see the whole system at once.
why: Likely reason: a diagram makes the flow of power from panels to grid easier to follow than tables.
how: Reads outputs and inputs from the store and works out a cost for each box. It builds boxes for modules, inverters, electrical BOS and grid, adds storage and total boxes when relevant, and draws arrows between them. Clicking a box records it as selected so its details can be shown.
inputs: outputs and inputs from the store, plus clicks on the boxes.
outputs: A diagram on screen and the details of the selected box.
risks: Only four of seven sections were available to review. Box positions and costs are captured when the diagram first draws, so changes made while it is open may not appear.
debug: If box costs look wrong, compare them with the results tab. If arrows are missing, check whether storage is on. If the array area looks far off, check the unit assumption in the module details.
